summary: iter183 — Offline-First system E2E validated. IndexedDB outbox (smartprov-outbox/registrations v1) is created on PWA boot. Enqueue→pending→syncAll→status transitions all work. OfflineQueueBadge compact pill shows 'Offline' when offline (yellow) and 'N pendentes' when online with items (blue), and is hidden when empty+online. Expanded panel exposes sync-btn / close / per-item discard with correct data-testids. Sync engine correctly POSTs to /api/rede-ia/public/ctos/{collab_id} and updates status to failed/conflict/synced based on HTTP response. Backend endpoint validated with 5/5 pytest passing (happy path + 3 validation errors + persistence check). Service Worker registration is gated by NODE_ENV==='production' in /src/index.js:17, so in the preview (dev server) the SW is NOT registered and TILE_CACHE cannot be validated E2E in preview — code in /public/service-worker.js itself is correct and will work in prod build.

integration_issues.issue: In the preview environment the frontend runs via 'craco start' (dev), so NODE_ENV !== 'production' and the SW registration block at /app/frontend/src/index.js:17 is skipped. navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistration() returns null and caches.keys() is empty. This means TILE_CACHE 'smartprov-tiles-v1' is never populated in preview, so test #8 (map tiles surviving offline) cannot be validated here. The SW file itself (/public/service-worker.js) is served correctly (200 OK) and the code is logically sound; in a production build (yarn build → serve) it will register and cache tiles as designed. RECOMMENDATION (optional): allow SW registration when REACT_APP_ENABLE_SW=1 even in dev, OR document that tile-cache validation must be performed against a prod build.

action_items: (Optional) Relax SW registration gate in /app/frontend/src/index.js to allow opt-in registration in dev (e.g. via REACT_APP_ENABLE_SW=1) so that the offline tile-cache feature can be validated end-to-end in the preview environment. In production builds this already works.

(Already verified static) Confirm via production deploy that map tiles in /app/frontend/src/CadastroCTOWizard.js Step 2 actually use one of the TILE_HOSTS listed in service-worker.js (tile.openstreetmap.org, basemaps.cartocdn.com, etc) — otherwise STALE-WHILE-REVALIDATE won't engage.

(Optional UX) /app/frontend/src/OfflineQueueBadge.js line ~98–104: when offline AND there are pending items, pill text concatenates 'Offline' + 'N pendente(s)' without a separator, rendering as 'Offline1 pendente'. Add a space/comma between the two states for readability.
critical_code_review_comments: offlineQueue.js is clean (296 lines): well-segmented (CRUD / events / sync engine / autosync), uses indexes (status, created_at, collab_id) for fast queries, in-flight guard via _syncInFlight prevents duplicate sync passes, and 409→'conflict' is handled distinctly from generic failures. Good.

OfflineQueueBadge.js (256 lines): correct re-render on outbox.onChange + online/offline events; the compact pill is hidden when there are zero pending AND online — matches spec. Minor cosmetic: pill text in offline+pending state concatenates without space (see action item).

service-worker.js (142 lines): correct strategy split (NETWORK-FIRST for navigation; CACHE-FIRST for /static; STALE-WHILE-REVALIDATE for TILE_HOSTS; never cache /api/). activate handler preserves TILE_CACHE across CACHE_NAME bumps — exactly the right pattern for keeping field tiles after redeploys. skipWaiting + clients.claim avoids the 'need ctrl+shift+R' bug.
index.js:17 — SW registration is correctly gated to production, which is CRA's default safety. The downside is preview-time validation, see action items.

Backend /api/rede-ia/public/ctos/{collab_id} returns proper 400/404 with descriptive messages; sigla is normalized to remove accents (resilient to old app versions). cto_ports are synced after creation — verified the created CTO appears immediately in the public list endpoint.

rca of the issue: Test 7/8 (SW + tile cache) — RCA: /app/frontend/src/index.js line 17 gates SW registration with `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'`. The preview runs `craco start` (dev server) so NODE_ENV='development' and the registration block is skipped. Verified by: (1) navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistration() === null at runtime, (2) caches.keys() returns [] at runtime, (3) static file curl of /service-worker.js returns 200 with correct payload — i.e. the file is deployable, only the registration is gated. Mitigation: either add an opt-in env flag (REACT_APP_ENABLE_SW=1) to the gate, or only validate this feature against a production build.
